historical_record.description: Balboa High School, designed by John Bakewell Jr.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 205, Balboa High School.

The first unit of Balboa High School — the academic building and shops — was built to designs by the city architect John Reid Jr., for a Spanish Colonial Revival school laid out for fresh air and sunshine and named for Vasco Núñez de Balboa.
The second unit — gymnasia, cafeteria and a shop addition — was built to designs by Samuel Lightner Hyman and A. Appleton.
The third unit — an academic building, auditorium and athletic field — was built to designs by Bakewell & Weihe; the whole school had cost almost $1.5 million when it was completed in 1934.
The school opened with 653 students and 23 teachers. Its later graduates include the conductor Calvin Simmons, the science-fiction writer Forrest Ackerman and Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead.
